etad vyāptimad eteṣāṃ sarvabhūtāśritaṃ vapuḥ ||
verses.translation: Goodness is declared (to have the form of) knowledge, Darkness (of) ignorance, Activity (of) love and hatred; such is the nature of these (three) which is (all-) pervading and clings to everything created.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र यत् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं किञ्चिद् आत्मनि लक्षयेत् ।
प्रशान्तम् इव शुद्धाभं सत्त्वं तद् उपधारयेत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
tatra yat prītisaṃyuktaṃ kiñcid ātmani lakṣayet |
praśāntam iva śuddhābhaṃ sattvaṃ tad upadhārayet ||
verses.translation: When (man) experiences in his soul a (feeling) full of bliss, a deep calm, as it were, and a pure light, then let him know (that it is) among those three (the quality called) Goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
यत् तु दुःखसमायुक्तम् अप्रीतिकरम् आत्मनः ।
तद् रजो ऽप्रतिपं विद्यात् सततं हर्तृ देहिनाम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yat tu duḥkhasamāyuktam aprītikaram ātmanaḥ |
tad rajo 'pratipaṃ vidyāt satataṃ hartṛ dehinām ||
verses.translation: What is mixed with pain and does not give satisfaction to the soul one may know (to be the quality of) Activity, which is difficult to conquer, and which ever draws embodied (souls towards sensual objects).

verses.sanskrit:
यत् तु स्यान् मोहसंयुक्तम् अव्यक्तं विषयात्मकम् ।
अप्रतर्क्यम् अविज्ञेयं तमस् तद् उपधारयेत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yat tu syān mohasaṃyuktam avyaktaṃ viṣayātmakam |
apratarkyam avijñeyaṃ tamas tad upadhārayet ||
verses.translation: What is coupled with delusion, what has the character of an undiscernible mass, what cannot be fathomed by reasoning, what cannot be fully known, one must consider (as the quality of) Darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयाणाम् अपि चैतेषां गुणानां यः फलोदयः ।
अग्र्यो मध्यो जघन्यश् च तं प्रवक्ष्याम्य् अशेषतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
trayāṇām api caiteṣāṃ guṇānāṃ yaḥ phalodayaḥ |
agryo madhyo jaghanyaś ca taṃ pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ ||
verses.translation: I will, moreover, fully describe the results which arise from these three qualities, the excellent ones, the middling ones, and the lowest.

verses.sanskrit:
वेदाभ्यासस् तपो ज्ञानं शौचम् इन्द्रियनिग्रहः ।
धर्मक्रियात्मचिन्ता च सात्त्विकं गुणलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
vedābhyāsas tapo jñānaṃ śaucam indriyanigrahaḥ |
dharmakriyātmacintā ca sāttvikaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: The study of the Vedas, austerity, (the pursuit of) knowledge, purity, control over the organs, the performance of meritorious acts and meditation on the Soul, (are) the marks of the quality of Goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
आरम्भरुचिताधर्यम् असत्कार्यपरिग्रहः ।
विषयोपसेवा चाजस्रं राजसं गुणलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ārambharucitādharyam asatkāryaparigrahaḥ |
viṣayopasevā cājasraṃ rājasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: Delighting in undertakings, want of firmness, commission of sinful acts, and continual indulgence in sensual pleasures, (are) the marks of the quality of Activity.

verses.sanskrit:
लोभः स्वप्नो ऽघृतिः क्रौर्यं नास्तिक्यं भिन्नवृत्तिता ।
याचिष्णुता प्रमादश् च तामसं गुणलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
lobhaḥ svapno 'ghṛtiḥ krauryaṃ nāstikyaṃ bhinnavṛttitā |
yāciṣṇutā pramādaś ca tāmasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: Covetousness, sleepiness, pusillanimity, cruelty, atheism, leading an evil life, a habit of soliciting favours, and inattentiveness, are the marks of the quality of Darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयाणाम् अपि चैतेषां गुणानां त्रिषु तिष्ठताम् ।
इदं सामासिकं ज्ञेयं क्रमशो गुणलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
trayāṇām api caiteṣāṃ guṇānāṃ triṣu tiṣṭhatām |
idaṃ sāmāsikaṃ jñeyaṃ kramaśo guṇalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: Know, moreover, the following to be a brief description of the three qualities, each in its order, as they appear in the three (times, the present, past, and future).

verses.sanskrit:
यत् कर्म कृत्वा कुर्वंश् च करिष्यंश् चैव लज्जति ।
तज् ज्ञेयं विदुषा सर्वं तामसं गुणलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yat karma kṛtvā kurvaṃś ca kariṣyaṃś caiva lajjati |
taj jñeyaṃ viduṣā sarvaṃ tāmasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: When a (man), having done, doing, or being about to do any act, feels ashamed, the learned may know that all (such acts bear) the mark of the quality of Darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
येनास्मिन् कर्मणा लोके ख्यातिम् इच्छन्ति पुष्कलाम् ।
न च शोचत्य् असम्पत्तौ तद् विज्ञेयं तु राजसम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yenāsmin karmaṇā loke khyātim icchanti puṣkalām |
na ca śocaty asampattau tad vijñeyaṃ tu rājasam ||
verses.translation: But, when (a man) desires (to gain) by an act much fame in this world and feels no sorrow on failing, know that it (bears the mark of the quality of) Activity.

verses.sanskrit:
यत् सर्वेणेच्छति ज्ञातुं यन् न लज्जति चाचरन् ।
येन तुष्यति चात्मास्य तत् सत्त्वगुणलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yat sarveṇecchati jñātuṃ yan na lajjati cācaran |
yena tuṣyati cātmāsya tat sattvaguṇalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: But that (bears) the mark of the quality of Goodness which with his whole (heart) he desires to know, which he is not ashamed to perform, and at which his soul rejoices.

verses.sanskrit:
तमसो लक्षणं कामो रजसस् त्व् अर्थ उच्यते ।
सत्त्वस्य लक्षणं धर्मः श्रैष्ठ्यम् एषां यथोत्तरम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
tamaso lakṣaṇaṃ kāmo rajasas tv artha ucyate |
sattvasya lakṣaṇaṃ dharmaḥ śraiṣṭhyam eṣāṃ yathottaram ||
verses.translation: The craving after sensual pleasures is declared to be the mark of Darkness, (the pursuit of) wealth (the mark) of Activity, (the desire to gain) spiritual merit the mark of Goodness; each later) named quality is) better than the preceding one.

verses.sanskrit:
येन यांस् तु गुणेनैषां संसारान् प्रतिपद्यते ।
तान् समासेन वक्ष्यामि सर्वस्यास्य यथाक्रमम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yena yāṃs tu guṇenaiṣāṃ saṃsārān pratipadyate |
tān samāsena vakṣyāmi sarvasyāsya yathākramam ||
verses.translation: I will briefly declare in due order what transmigrations in this whole (world a man) obtains through each of these qualities.

verses.sanskrit:
देवत्वं सात्त्विका यान्ति मनुष्यत्वं च राजसाः ।
तिर्यक्त्वं तामसा नित्यम् इत्य् एषा त्रिविधा गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
devatvaṃ sāttvikā yānti manuṣyatvaṃ ca rājasāḥ |
tiryaktvaṃ tāmasā nityam ity eṣā trividhā gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Those endowed with Goodness reach the state of gods, those endowed with Activity the state of men, and those endowed with Darkness ever sink to the condition of beasts; that is the threefold course of transmigrations.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिविधा त्रिविधैषा तु विज्ञेया गौणिकी गतिः ।
अधमा मध्यमाग्र्या च कर्मविद्या विशेषतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
trividhā trividhaiṣā tu vijñeyā gauṇikī gatiḥ |
adhamā madhyamāgryā ca karmavidyā viśeṣataḥ ||
verses.translation: But know this threefold course of transmigrations that depends on the (three) qualities (to be again) threefold, low, middling, and high, according to the particular nature of the acts and of the knowledge (of each man).

verses.sanskrit:
स्थावराः कृमिकीटाश् च मत्स्याः सर्पाः सकच्छपाः ।
पशवश् च मृगाश् चैव जघन्या तामसी गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
sthāvarāḥ kṛmikīṭāś ca matsyāḥ sarpāḥ sakacchapāḥ |
paśavaś ca mṛgāś caiva jaghanyā tāmasī gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Immovable (beings), insects, both small and great, fishes, snakes, and tortoises, cattle and wild animals, are the lowest conditions to which (the quality of) Darkness leads.

verses.sanskrit:
हस्तिनश् च तुरङ्गाश् च शूद्रा म्लेच्छाश् च गर्हिताः ।
सिंहा व्याघ्रा वराहाश् च मध्यमा तामसी गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
hastinaś ca turaṅgāś ca śūdrā mlecchāś ca garhitāḥ |
siṃhā vyāghrā varāhāś ca madhyamā tāmasī gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Elephants, horses, Sudras, and despicable barbarians, lions, tigers, and boars (are) the middling states, caused by (the quality of) Darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
चारणाश् च सुपर्णाश् च पुरुषाश् चैव दाम्भिकाः ।
रक्षांसि च पिशाचाश् च तामसीषूत्तमा गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
cāraṇāś ca suparṇāś ca puruṣāś caiva dāmbhikāḥ |
rakṣāṃsi ca piśācāś ca tāmasīṣūttamā gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Karanas, Suparnas and hypocrites, Rakshasas and Pisakas (belong to) the highest (rank of) conditions among those produced by Darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
झल्ला मल्ला नटाश् चैव पुरुषाः शस्त्रवृत्तयः ।
द्यूतपानप्रसक्ताश् च जघन्या राजसी गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
jhallā mallā naṭāś caiva puruṣāḥ śastravṛttayaḥ |
dyūtapānaprasaktāś ca jaghanyā rājasī gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Ghallas, Mallas, Natas, men who subsist by despicable occupations and those addicted to gambling and drinking (form) the lowest (order of) conditions caused by Activity.

verses.sanskrit:
राजानः क्षत्रियाश् चैव राज्ञां चैव पुरोहिताः ।
वादयुद्धप्रधानाश् च मध्यमा राजसी गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
rājānaḥ kṣatriyāś caiva rājñāṃ caiva purohitāḥ |
vādayuddhapradhānāś ca madhyamā rājasī gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Kings and Kshatriyas, the domestic priests of kings, and those who delight in the warfare of disputations (constitute) the middling (rank of the) states caused by Activity.

verses.sanskrit:
गन्धर्वा गुह्यका यक्षा विबुधानुचराश् च ये ।
तथैवाप्सरसः सर्वा राजसीषूत्तमा गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
gandharvā guhyakā yakṣā vibudhānucarāś ca ye |
tathaivāpsarasaḥ sarvā rājasīṣūttamā gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Gandharvas, the Guhyakas, and the servants of the gods, likewise the Apsarases, (belong all to) the highest (rank of) conditions produced by Activity.

verses.sanskrit:
तापसा यतयो विप्रा ये च वैमानिका गणाः ।
नक्षत्राणि च दैत्याश् च प्रथमा सात्त्विकी गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
tāpasā yatayo viprā ye ca vaimānikā gaṇāḥ |
nakṣatrāṇi ca daityāś ca prathamā sāttvikī gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Hermits, ascetics, Brahmanas, the crowds of the Vaimanika deities, the lunar mansions, and the Daityas (form) the first (and lowest rank of the) existences caused by Goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
यज्वान ऋषयो देवा वेदा ज्योतींषि वत्सराः ।
पितरश् चैव साध्याश् च द्वितीया सात्त्विकी गतिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yajvāna ṛṣayo devā vedā jyotīṃṣi vatsarāḥ |
pitaraś caiva sādhyāś ca dvitīyā sāttvikī gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Sacrificers, the sages, the gods, the Vedas, the heavenly lights, the years, the manes, and the Sadhyas (constitute) the second order of existences, caused by Goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मा विश्वसृजो धर्मो महान् अव्यक्तम् एव च ।
उत्तमां सात्त्विकीम् एतां गतिम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥
verses.transliteration:
brahmā viśvasṛjo dharmo mahān avyaktam eva ca |
uttamāṃ sāttvikīm etāṃ gatim āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
verses.translation: The sages declare Brahma, the creators of the universe, the law, the Great One, and the Undiscernible One (to constitute) the highest order of beings produced by Goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
एष सर्वः समुद्दिष्टस् त्रिःप्रकारस्य कर्मणः ।
त्रिविधस् त्रिविधः कृत्स्नः संसारः सार्वभौतिकः ॥
verses.transliteration:
eṣa sarvaḥ samuddiṣṭas triḥprakārasya karmaṇaḥ |
trividhas trividhaḥ kṛtsnaḥ saṃsāraḥ sārvabhautikaḥ ||
verses.translation: Thus (the result) of the threefold action, the whole system of transmigrations which (consists) of three classes, (each) with three subdivisions, and which includes all created beings, has been fully pointed out.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन धर्मस्यासेवनेन च ।
पापान् संयान्ति संसारान् अविद्वांसो नराधमाः ॥
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena dharmasyāsevanena ca |
pāpān saṃyānti saṃsārān avidvāṃso narādhamāḥ ||
verses.translation: In consequence of attachment to (the objects of) the senses, and in consequence of the non-performance of their duties, fools, the lowest of men, reach the vilest births.

verses.sanskrit:
यां यां योनिं तु जीवो ऽयं येन येनेह कर्मणा ।
क्रमशो याति लोके ऽस्मिंस् तत् तत् सर्वं निबोधत ॥
verses.transliteration:
yāṃ yāṃ yoniṃ tu jīvo 'yaṃ yena yeneha karmaṇā |
kramaśo yāti loke 'smiṃs tat tat sarvaṃ nibodhata ||
verses.translation: What wombs this individual soul enters in this world and in consequence of what actions, learn the particulars of that at large and in due order.

verses.sanskrit:
बहून् वर्षगणान् घोरान् नरकान् प्राप्य तत्क्षयात् ।
संशारान् प्रतिपद्यन्ते महापातकिनस् त्व् इमान् ॥
verses.transliteration:
bahūn varṣagaṇān ghorān narakān prāpya tatkṣayāt |
saṃśārān pratipadyante mahāpātakinas tv imān ||
verses.translation: Those who committed mortal sins (mahapataka), having passed during large numbers of years through dreadful hells, obtain, after the expiration of (that term of punishment), the following births.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वसूकरखरोष्ट्राणां गोऽजाविमृगमक्षिणाम् ।
चण्डालपुक्कसानां च ब्रह्महा योनिम् ऋच्छति ॥
verses.transliteration:
śvasūkarakharoṣṭrāṇāṃ go'jāvimṛgamakṣiṇām |
caṇḍālapukkasānāṃ ca brahmahā yonim ṛcchati ||
verses.translation: The slayer of a Brahmana enters the womb of a dog, a pig, an ass, a camel, a cow, a goat, a sheep, a deer, a bird, a Kandala, and a Pukkasa.

verses.sanskrit:
कृमिकीटपतङ्गानां विड्भुजां चैव पक्षिणाम् ।
हिंस्राणां चैव सत्त्वानां सुरापो ब्राह्मणो व्रजेत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
kṛmikīṭapataṅgānāṃ viḍbhujāṃ caiva pakṣiṇām |
hiṃsrāṇāṃ caiva sattvānāṃ surāpo brāhmaṇo vrajet ||
verses.translation: A Brahmana who drinks (the spirituous liquor called) Sura shall enter (the bodies) of small and large insects, of moths, of birds, feeding on ordure, and of destructive beasts.

verses.sanskrit:
लूताहिसरटानां च तिरश्चां चाम्बुचारिणाम् ।
हिंस्राणां च पिशाचानां स्तेनो विप्रः सहस्रशः ॥
verses.transliteration:
lūtāhisaraṭānāṃ ca tiraścāṃ cāmbucāriṇām |
hiṃsrāṇāṃ ca piśācānāṃ steno vipraḥ sahasraśaḥ ||
verses.translation: A Brahmana who steals (the gold of a Brahmana shall pass) a thousand times (through the bodies) of spiders, snakes and lizards, of aquatic animals and of destructive Pisakas.

verses.sanskrit:
तृणगुल्मलतानां च क्रयादां दंष्ट्रिणाम् अपि ।
क्रूरकर्मकृतां चैव शतशो गुरुतल्पगः ॥
verses.transliteration:
tṛṇagulmalatānāṃ ca krayādāṃ daṃṣṭriṇām api |
krūrakarmakṛtāṃ caiva śataśo gurutalpagaḥ ||
verses.translation: The violator of a Guru's bed (enters) a hundred times (the forms) of grasses, shrubs, and creepers, likewise of carnivorous (animals) and of (beasts) with fangs and of those doing cruel deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
हिंस्रा भवन्ति क्रव्यादाः कृमयो ऽमेध्यभक्षिणः ।
परस्परादिनः स्तेनाः प्रेतान्त्यस्त्रीनिषेविणः ॥
verses.transliteration:
hiṃsrā bhavanti kravyādāḥ kṛmayo 'medhyabhakṣiṇaḥ |
parasparādinaḥ stenāḥ pretāntyastrīniṣeviṇaḥ ||
verses.translation: Men who delight in doing hurt (become) carnivorous (animals); those who eat forbidden food, worms; thieves, creatures consuming their own kind; those who have intercourse with women of the lowest castes, Pretas.

verses.sanskrit:
संयोगं पतितैर् गत्वा परस्यैव च योषितम् ।
अपहृत्य च विप्रस्वं भवति ब्रह्मराक्षसः ॥
verses.transliteration:
saṃyogaṃ patitair gatvā parasyaiva ca yoṣitam |
apahṛtya ca viprasvaṃ bhavati brahmarākṣasaḥ ||
verses.translation: He who has associated with outcasts, he who has approached the wives of other men, and he who has stolen the property of a Brahmana become Brahmarakshasas.

verses.sanskrit:
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानि हृत्वा लोभेन मानवः ।
विविधानि च रत्नानि जायते हेमकर्तृषु ॥
verses.transliteration:
maṇimuktāpravālāni hṛtvā lobhena mānavaḥ |
vividhāni ca ratnāni jāyate hemakartṛṣu ||
verses.translation: A man who out of greed has stolen gems, pearls or coral, or any of the many other kinds of precious things, is born among the goldsmiths.

verses.sanskrit:
धान्यं हृत्वा भवत्य् आखुः कांस्यं हंसो जलं प्लवः ।
मधु दंशः पयः काओ रसं श्वा नकुलो घृतम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
dhānyaṃ hṛtvā bhavaty ākhuḥ kāṃsyaṃ haṃso jalaṃ plavaḥ |
madhu daṃśaḥ payaḥ kāo rasaṃ śvā nakulo ghṛtam ||
verses.translation: For stealing grain (a man) becomes a rat, for stealing yellow metal a Hamsa, for stealing water a Plava, for stealing honey a stinging insect, for stealing milk a crow, for stealing condiments a dog, for stealing clarified butter an ichneumon;

verses.sanskrit:
मांसं गृध्रो वपां मद्गुस् तैलं तैलपकः खगः ।
चीरीवाकस् तु लवणं बलाका शकुनिर् दधि ॥
verses.transliteration:
māṃsaṃ gṛdhro vapāṃ madgus tailaṃ tailapakaḥ khagaḥ |
cīrīvākas tu lavaṇaṃ balākā śakunir dadhi ||
verses.translation: For stealing meat a vulture, for stealing fat a cormorant, for stealing oil a winged animal (of the kind called) Tailapaka, for stealing salt a cricket, for stealing sour milk a bird (of the kind called) Balaka.

verses.sanskrit:
कौशेयं तित्तिरिर् हृत्वा क्षौमं ह्र्त्वा तु दर्दुरः ।
कार्पासतान्तवं क्रौञ्चो गोधा गां वाग्गुदो गुडम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
kauśeyaṃ tittirir hṛtvā kṣaumaṃ hrtvā tu darduraḥ |
kārpāsatāntavaṃ krauñco godhā gāṃ vāggudo guḍam ||
verses.translation: For stealing silk a partridge, for stealing linen a frog, for stealing cotton-cloth a crane, for stealing a cow an iguana, for stealing molasses a flying-fox;

verses.sanskrit:
छुच्छुन्दरीः शुभान् गन्धान् पत्रशाकं तु बर्हिणः ।
श्वावित् कृतान्नं विविधम् कृतान्नं तु शल्यकः ॥
verses.transliteration:
chucchundarīḥ śubhān gandhān patraśākaṃ tu barhiṇaḥ |
śvāvit kṛtānnaṃ vividham kṛtānnaṃ tu śalyakaḥ ||
verses.translation: For stealing fine perfumes a musk-rat, for stealing vegetables consisting of leaves a peacock, for stealing cooked food of various kinds a porcupine, for stealing uncooked food a hedgehog.

verses.sanskrit:
बको भवति हृत्वाग्निं गृहकारी ह्य् उपस्करम् ।
रक्तानि हृत्वा वासांसि जायते जीवजीवकः ॥
verses.transliteration:
bako bhavati hṛtvāgniṃ gṛhakārī hy upaskaram |
raktāni hṛtvā vāsāṃsi jāyate jīvajīvakaḥ ||
verses.translation: For stealing fire he becomes a heron, for stealing household-utensils a mason-wasp, for stealing dyed clothes a francolin-partridge;

verses.sanskrit:
वृको मृगेभं व्याघ्रो ऽश्वं फलमूलं तु मर्कटः ।
स्त्रीम् ऋक्षः स्तोकको वारि यानान्य् उष्ट्रः पशून् अजः ॥
verses.transliteration:
vṛko mṛgebhaṃ vyāghro 'śvaṃ phalamūlaṃ tu markaṭaḥ |
strīm ṛkṣaḥ stokako vāri yānāny uṣṭraḥ paśūn ajaḥ ||
verses.translation: For stealing a deer or an elephant a wolf, for stealing a horse a tiger, for stealing fruit and roots a monkey, for stealing a woman a bear, for stealing water a black-white cuckoo, for stealing vehicles a camel, for stealing cattle a he-goat.

verses.sanskrit:
यद् वा तद् वा परद्रव्यम् अपहृत्य बलान् नरः ।
अवश्यं याति तिर्यक्त्वं जग्ध्वा चैवाहुतिं हविः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yad vā tad vā paradravyam apahṛtya balān naraḥ |
avaśyaṃ yāti tiryaktvaṃ jagdhvā caivāhutiṃ haviḥ ||
verses.translation: That man who has forcibly taken away any kind of property belonging to another, or who has eaten sacrificial food (of) which (no portion) had been offered, inevitably becomes an animal.

verses.sanskrit:
स्त्रियो ऽप्य् एतेन कल्पेन हृत्वा दोषम् अवाप्नुयुः ।
एतेषाम् एव जन्तूनां भार्यात्वम् उपयान्ति ताः ॥
verses.transliteration:
striyo 'py etena kalpena hṛtvā doṣam avāpnuyuḥ |
eteṣām eva jantūnāṃ bhāryātvam upayānti tāḥ ||
verses.translation: Women, also, who in like manner have committed a theft, shall incur guilt; they will become the females of those same creatures (which have been enumerated above).

verses.sanskrit:
स्वेभ्यः स्वेभ्यस् तु कर्मभ्यश् च्युता वर्णा ह्य् अनापदि ।
पापान् संसृत्य संसारान् प्रेष्यतां यान्ति दस्युषु ॥
verses.transliteration:
svebhyaḥ svebhyas tu karmabhyaś cyutā varṇā hy anāpadi |
pāpān saṃsṛtya saṃsārān preṣyatāṃ yānti dasyuṣu ||
verses.translation: But (men of the four) castes who have relinquished without the pressure of necessity their proper occupations, will become the servants of Dasyus, after migrating into despicable bodies.

verses.sanskrit:
वान्ताश्य् उल्कामुखः प्रेतो विप्रो धर्मात् स्वकाच् च्युतः ।
अमेध्यकुणपाशी च क्षत्रियः कूटपूत्नः ॥
verses.transliteration:
vāntāśy ulkāmukhaḥ preto vipro dharmāt svakāc cyutaḥ |
amedhyakuṇapāśī ca kṣatriyaḥ kūṭapūtnaḥ ||
verses.translation: A Brahmana who has fallen off from his duty (becomes) an Ulkamukha Preta, who feeds on what has been vomited; and a Kshatriya, a Kataputana (Preta), who eats impure substances and corpses.

verses.sanskrit:
मैत्राक्षिज्योतिकः प्रेतो वैश्यो भवति पूयभुक् ।
चैलाशकश् च भवति शूद्रो धर्मात् स्वकाच् च्युतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
maitrākṣijyotikaḥ preto vaiśyo bhavati pūyabhuk |
cailāśakaś ca bhavati śūdro dharmāt svakāc cyutaḥ ||
verses.translation: A Vaisya who has fallen off from his duty becomes a Maitrakshagyotika Preta, who feeds on pus; and a Sudra, a Kailasaka (Preta, who feeds on moths).

verses.sanskrit:
यथा यथा निषेवन्ते विषयान् विषयात्मकाः ।
तथा तथा कुशलता तेषां तेषूपजायते ॥
verses.transliteration:
yathā yathā niṣevante viṣayān viṣayātmakāḥ |
tathā tathā kuśalatā teṣāṃ teṣūpajāyate ||
verses.translation: In proportion as sensual men indulge in sensual pleasures, in that same proportion their taste for them grows.

verses.sanskrit:
ते ऽभ्यासात् कर्मणां तेषां पापानाम् अल्पबुद्धयः ।
सम्प्राप्नुवन्ति दुःखानि तासु तास्व् इह योनिषु ॥
verses.transliteration:
te 'bhyāsāt karmaṇāṃ teṣāṃ pāpānām alpabuddhayaḥ |
samprāpnuvanti duḥkhāni tāsu tāsv iha yoniṣu ||
verses.translation: By repeating their sinful acts those men of small understanding suffer pain here (below) in various births;

verses.sanskrit:
तामिस्रादिषु चोग्रेषु नरकेषु विवर्तनम् ।
असिपत्रवनादीनि बन्धच्छेदनानि च ॥
verses.transliteration:
tāmisrādiṣu cogreṣu narakeṣu vivartanam |
asipatravanādīni bandhacchedanāni ca ||
verses.translation: (The torture of) being tossed about in dreadful hells, Tamisra and the rest, (that of) the Forest with sword-leaved trees and the like, and (that of) being bound and mangled;

verses.sanskrit:
विविधाश् चैव सम्पीडाः काकोलूकश् च भक्षणम् ।
करम्भवालुकातापान् कुम्भीपाकांश् च दारुणान् ॥
verses.transliteration:
vividhāś caiva sampīḍāḥ kākolūkaś ca bhakṣaṇam |
karambhavālukātāpān kumbhīpākāṃś ca dāruṇān ||
verses.translation: And various torments, the (pain of) being devoured by ravens and owls, the heat of scorching sand, and the (torture of) being boiled in jars, which is hard to bear;

verses.sanskrit:
सम्भवांश् च वियोनीषु दुःखप्रायासु नित्यशः ।
शीतातपाभिघातांश् च विविधानि भयानि च ॥
verses.transliteration:
sambhavāṃś ca viyonīṣu duḥkhaprāyāsu nityaśaḥ |
śītātapābhighātāṃś ca vividhāni bhayāni ca ||
verses.translation: And births in the wombs (of) despicable (beings) which cause constant misery, and afflictions from cold and heat and terrors of various kinds,

verses.sanskrit:
असकृद् गर्भवासेषु वासं जन्म च दारुणम् ।
बन्धनानि च कष्टानि परप्रेष्यत्वम् एव च ॥
verses.transliteration:
asakṛd garbhavāseṣu vāsaṃ janma ca dāruṇam |
bandhanāni ca kaṣṭāni parapreṣyatvam eva ca ||
verses.translation: The (pain of) repeatedly lying in various wombs and agonizing births, imprisonment in fetters hard to bear, and the misery of being enslaved by others,

verses.sanskrit:
बन्धुप्रियवियोगांश् च संवासं चैव दुर्जनैः ।
द्रव्यार्जनं च नाशं च मित्रामित्रस्य चार्जनम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
bandhupriyaviyogāṃś ca saṃvāsaṃ caiva durjanaiḥ |
dravyārjanaṃ ca nāśaṃ ca mitrāmitrasya cārjanam ||
verses.translation: And separations from their relatives and dear ones, and the (pain of) dwelling together with the wicked, (labour in) gaining wealth and its loss, (trouble in) making friends and (the appearance of) enemies,

verses.sanskrit:
जरां चैवाप्रतीकारां व्याधिभिश् चोपपीडनम् ।
क्लेशांश् च विविधांस् तांस् तान् मृत्युम् एव च दुर्जनम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
jarāṃ caivāpratīkārāṃ vyādhibhiś copapīḍanam |
kleśāṃś ca vividhāṃs tāṃs tān mṛtyum eva ca durjanam ||
verses.translation: Old age against which there is no remedy, the pangs of diseases, afflictions of many various kinds, and (finally) unconquerable death.

verses.sanskrit:
यादृशेन तु भावेन यद् यत् कर्म निषेवते ।
तादृशेन शरीरेण तत् तत् फलम् उपाश्नुते ॥
verses.transliteration:
yādṛśena tu bhāvena yad yat karma niṣevate |
tādṛśena śarīreṇa tat tat phalam upāśnute ||
verses.translation: But with whatever disposition of mind (a man) forms any act, he reaps its result in a (future) body endowed with the same quality.

verses.sanskrit:
एष सर्वः समुद्दिष्टः कर्मणां वः फलोदयः ।
नैःश्रेयसकरं कर्म विप्रस्येदं निबोधत ॥
verses.transliteration:
eṣa sarvaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ karmaṇāṃ vaḥ phalodayaḥ |
naiḥśreyasakaraṃ karma viprasyedaṃ nibodhata ||
verses.translation: All the results, proceeding from actions, have been thus pointed out; learn (next) those acts which secure supreme bliss to a Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit:
वेदाभ्यासस् तपो ज्ञानम् इन्दिर्याणां च संयमः ।
अहिंसा गुरुसेवा च निःश्रेयसकरं परम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
vedābhyāsas tapo jñānam indiryāṇāṃ ca saṃyamaḥ |
ahiṃsā gurusevā ca niḥśreyasakaraṃ param ||
verses.translation: Studying the Veda, (practising) austerities, (the acquisition of true) knowledge, the subjugation of the organs, abstention from doing injury, and serving the Guru are the best means for attaining supreme bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषाम् अपि चैतेषां शुभानाम् इह कर्मणाम् ।
किञ्चिच् छ्रेयस्करतरं कर्मोक्तं पुरुषं प्रति ॥
verses.transliteration:
sarveṣām api caiteṣāṃ śubhānām iha karmaṇām |
kiñcic chreyaskarataraṃ karmoktaṃ puruṣaṃ prati ||
verses.translation: (If you ask) whether among all these virtuous actions, (performed) here below, (there be) one which has been declared more efficacious (than the rest) for securing supreme happiness to man,

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषाम् अपि चैतेषाम् आत्मज्ञानं परं स्मृतम् ।
तद् ध्य् अग्र्यं सर्वविद्यानां प्राप्यते ह्य् अमृतं ततः ॥
verses.transliteration:
sarveṣām api caiteṣām ātmajñānaṃ paraṃ smṛtam |
tad dhy agryaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ prāpyate hy amṛtaṃ tataḥ ||
verses.translation: (The answer is that) the knowledge of the Soul is stated to be the most excellent among all of them; for that is the first of all sciences, because immortality is gained through that.

verses.sanskrit:
षण्णाम् एषां तु पूर्वेषां कर्मणां प्रेत्य चेह च ।
श्रेयस्करतरं ज्ञेयं सर्वदा कर्म वैदिकम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ṣaṇṇām eṣāṃ tu pūrveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ pretya ceha ca |
śreyaskarataraṃ jñeyaṃ sarvadā karma vaidikam ||
verses.translation: Among those six (kinds of) actions (enumerated) above, the performance of) the acts taught in the Veda must ever be held to be most efficacious for ensuring happiness in this world and the next.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदिके कर्मयोगे तु सर्वाण्य् एतान्य् अशेषतः ।
अन्तर्भवन्ति क्रमशस् तस्मिंस् तस्मिन् क्रियाविधौ ॥
verses.transliteration:
vaidike karmayoge tu sarvāṇy etāny aśeṣataḥ |
antarbhavanti kramaśas tasmiṃs tasmin kriyāvidhau ||
verses.translation: For in the performance of the acts prescribed by the Veda all those (others) are fully comprised, (each) in its turn in the several rules for the rites.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखाभ्युदयिकं चैव नैःश्रेयसिकम् एव च ।
प्रवृत्तं च निवृत्तं च द्विविधं कर्म वैदिकम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
sukhābhyudayikaṃ caiva naiḥśreyasikam eva ca |
pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttaṃ ca dvividhaṃ karma vaidikam ||
verses.translation: The acts prescribed by the Veda are of two kinds, such as procure an increase of happiness and cause a continuation (of mundane existence, pravritta), and such as ensure supreme bliss and cause a cessation (of mundane existence, nivritta).

verses.sanskrit:
इह चामुत्र वा काम्यं प्रवृत्तं कर्म कीर्त्यते ।
निष्कामं ज्ञानपूर्वं तु निवृत्तम् उपदिश्यते ॥
verses.transliteration:
iha cāmutra vā kāmyaṃ pravṛttaṃ karma kīrtyate |
niṣkāmaṃ jñānapūrvaṃ tu nivṛttam upadiśyate ||
verses.translation: Acts which secure (the fulfilment of) wishes in this world or in the next are called pravritta (such as cause a continuation of mundane existence); but acts performed without any desire (for a reward), preceded by (the acquisition) of (true) knowledge, are declared to be nivritta (such as cause the cessation of mundane existence).

verses.sanskrit:
प्रवृत्तं कर्म संसेव्यं देवानां एति साम्यताम् ।
निवृत्तं सेवमानस् तु भूतान्य् अत्येति पञ्च वै ॥
verses.transliteration:
pravṛttaṃ karma saṃsevyaṃ devānāṃ eti sāmyatām |
nivṛttaṃ sevamānas tu bhūtāny atyeti pañca vai ||
verses.translation: He who sedulously performs acts leading to future births (pravritta) becomes equal to the gods; but he who is intent on the performance of those causing the cessation (of existence, nivritta) indeed, passes beyond (the reach of) the five elements.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
समं पश्यन्न् आत्मयाजी स्वाराज्यम् अधिगच्छति ॥
verses.transliteration:
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani |
samaṃ paśyann ātmayājī svārājyam adhigacchati ||
verses.translation: He who sacrifices to the Self (alone), equally recognising the Self in all created beings and all created beings in the Self, becomes (independent like) an autocrat and self-luminous.

verses.sanskrit:
यथोक्तान्य् अपि कर्माणि परिहाय द्विजोत्तमः ।
आत्मज्ञाने शमे च स्याद् वेदाभ्यासे च यत्नवान् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yathoktāny api karmāṇi parihāya dvijottamaḥ |
ātmajñāne śame ca syād vedābhyāse ca yatnavān ||
verses.translation: After giving up even the above-mentioned sacrificial rites, a Brahmana should exert himself in (acquiring) the knowledge of the Soul, in extinguishing his passions, and in studying the Veda.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद् धि जन्मसाफल्यं ब्राह्मण्स्य विशेषतः ।
प्राप्यैतत् कृतकृत्यो हि द्विजो भवति नान्यथा ॥
verses.transliteration:
etad dhi janmasāphalyaṃ brāhmaṇsya viśeṣataḥ |
prāpyaitat kṛtakṛtyo hi dvijo bhavati nānyathā ||
verses.translation: For that secures the attainment of the object of existence, especially in the case of a Brahmana, because by attaining that, not otherwise, a twice-born man has gained all his ends.

verses.sanskrit:
पितृदेवमनुष्याणां वेदश् चक्षुः सनातनम् ।
अशक्यं चाप्रमेयं च वेदशास्त्रम् इति स्थितिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
pitṛdevamanuṣyāṇāṃ vedaś cakṣuḥ sanātanam |
aśakyaṃ cāprameyaṃ ca vedaśāstram iti sthitiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Veda is the eternal eye of the manes, gods, and men; the Veda-ordinance (is) both beyond the sphere of (human) power, and beyond the sphere of (human) comprehension; that is a certain fact.

verses.sanskrit:
या वेदबाह्याः श्रुतयो याश् च काश् च कुदृष्टयः ।
सर्वास् ता निष्फलाः प्रेत्य तमोनिष्ठा हि ताः स्मृताः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yā vedabāhyāḥ śrutayo yāś ca kāś ca kudṛṣṭayaḥ |
sarvās tā niṣphalāḥ pretya tamoniṣṭhā hi tāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
verses.translation: All those traditions (smriti) and those despicable systems of philosophy, which are not based on the Veda, produce no reward after death; for they are declared to be founded on Darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पद्यन्ते विनश्यन्ति यान्य् अतो ऽन्यानि कानिचित् ।
तान्य् अर्वाक्कालिकतया निष्फलान्य् अनृतानि च ॥
verses.transliteration:
utpadyante vinaśyanti yāny ato 'nyāni kānicit |
tāny arvākkālikatayā niṣphalāny anṛtāni ca ||
verses.translation: All those (doctrines), differing from the (Veda), which spring up and (soon) perish, are worthless and false, because they are of modern date.

verses.sanskrit:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं त्रयो लोकाश् चत्वारश् चाश्रमाः पृथक् ।
भूतं भवत् भविष्यं च सर्वं वेदात् प्रसिध्यति ॥
verses.transliteration:
cāturvarṇyaṃ trayo lokāś catvāraś cāśramāḥ pṛthak |
bhūtaṃ bhavat bhaviṣyaṃ ca sarvaṃ vedāt prasidhyati ||
verses.translation: The four castes, the three worlds, the four orders, the past, the present, and the future are all severally known by means of the Veda.

verses.sanskrit:
शब्दः स्पर्शश् च रूपं च रसो गन्धश् च पञ्चमः ।
वेदाद् एव प्रसूयन्ते प्रसूतिर् गुणकर्मतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ |
vedād eva prasūyante prasūtir guṇakarmataḥ ||
verses.translation: Sound, touch, colour, taste, and fifthly smell are known through the Veda alone, (their) production (is) through the (Vedic rites, which in this respect are) secondary acts.

verses.sanskrit:
बिभर्ति सर्वभूतानि वेदशास्त्रं सनातनम् ।
तस्माद् एतत् परं मन्ये यज् जन्तोर् अस्य साधनम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
bibharti sarvabhūtāni vedaśāstraṃ sanātanam |
tasmād etat paraṃ manye yaj jantor asya sādhanam ||
verses.translation: The eternal lore of the Veda upholds all created beings; hence I hold that to be supreme, which is the means of (securing happiness to) these creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
सैनापत्यं राज्यं च दण्डनेतृत्वम् एव च ।
सर्वलोकाधिपत्यं च वेदशास्त्रविद् अर्हति ॥
verses.transliteration:
saināpatyaṃ rājyaṃ ca daṇḍanetṛtvam eva ca |
sarvalokādhipatyaṃ ca vedaśāstravid arhati ||
verses.translation: Command of armies, royal authority, the office of a judge, and sovereignty over the whole world he (only) deserves who knows the Veda-science.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा जातबलो वह्निर् दहत्य् आर्द्रान् अपि द्रुमान् ।
तथा दहति वेदज्ञः कर्मजं दोषम् आत्मनः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yathā jātabalo vahnir dahaty ārdrān api drumān |
tathā dahati vedajñaḥ karmajaṃ doṣam ātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: As a fire that has gained strength consumes even trees full of sap, even so he who knows the Veda burns out the taint of his soul which arises from (evil) acts.

verses.sanskrit:
वेदशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञो यत्र तत्राश्रमे वसन् ।
इहैव लोके तिष्ठन् स ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
verses.transliteration:
vedaśāstrārthatattvajño yatra tatrāśrame vasan |
ihaiva loke tiṣṭhan sa brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: In whatever order (a man) who knows the true meaning of the Veda-science may dwell, he becomes even while abiding in this world, fit for the union with Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञेभ्यो ग्रन्थिनः श्रेष्ठा ग्रन्थिभ्यो धारिणो वराः ।
धारिभ्यो ज्ञानिनः श्रेष्ठा ज्ञानिभ्यो व्यवसायिनः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ajñebhyo granthinaḥ śreṣṭhā granthibhyo dhāriṇo varāḥ |
dhāribhyo jñāninaḥ śreṣṭhā jñānibhyo vyavasāyinaḥ ||
verses.translation: (Even forgetful) students of the (sacred) books are more distinguished than the ignorant, those who remember them surpass the (forgetful) students, those who possess a knowledge (of the meaning) are more distinguished than those who (only) remember (the words), men who follow (the teaching of the texts) surpass those who (merely) know (their meaning).

verses.sanskrit:
तपो विद्या च विप्रस्य निःश्रेयसकरं परम् ।
तपसा किल्बिषं हन्ति विद्ययामृतम् अश्नुते ॥
verses.transliteration:
tapo vidyā ca viprasya niḥśreyasakaraṃ param |
tapasā kilbiṣaṃ hanti vidyayāmṛtam aśnute ||
verses.translation: Austerity and sacred learning are the best means by which a Brahmana secures supreme bliss; by austerities he destroys guilt, by sacred learning he obtains the cessation of (births and) deaths.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्यक्षं चानुमानं च शास्त्रं च विविधागमम् ।
त्रयं सुविदितं कार्यं धर्मशुद्धिम् अभीप्सता ॥
verses.transliteration:
pratyakṣaṃ cānumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhāgamam |
trayaṃ suviditaṃ kāryaṃ dharmaśuddhim abhīpsatā ||
verses.translation: The three (kinds of evidence), perception, inference, and the (sacred) Institutes which comprise the tradition (of) many (schools), must be fully understood by him who desires perfect correctness with respect to the sacred law.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्षं धर्मोपदेशं च वेदशास्त्राविरोधिना ।
यस् तर्केणानुसन्धत्ते स धर्मं वेद नेतरः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ārṣaṃ dharmopadeśaṃ ca vedaśāstrāvirodhinā |
yas tarkeṇānusandhatte sa dharmaṃ veda netaraḥ ||
verses.translation: He alone, and no other man, knows the sacred law, who explores the (utterances) of the sages and the body of the laws, by (modes of) reasoning, not repugnant to the Veda-lore.

verses.sanskrit:
नैःश्रेयसम् इदं कर्म यथोदितम् अशेषतः ।
मानवस्यास्य शास्त्रस्य रहस्यम् उपदेक्ष्यते ॥
verses.transliteration:
naiḥśreyasam idaṃ karma yathoditam aśeṣataḥ |
mānavasyāsya śāstrasya rahasyam upadekṣyate ||
verses.translation: Thus the acts which secure supreme bliss have been exactly and fully described; (now) the secret portion of these Institutes, proclaimed by Manu, will be taught.

verses.sanskrit:
अनाम्नातेषु धर्मेषु कथं स्याद् इति चेद् भवेत् ।
यं शिष्टा ब्राह्मणा ब्रूयुः स धर्मः स्याद् अशङ्कितः ॥
verses.transliteration:
anāmnāteṣu dharmeṣu kathaṃ syād iti ced bhavet |
yaṃ śiṣṭā brāhmaṇā brūyuḥ sa dharmaḥ syād aśaṅkitaḥ ||
verses.translation: If it be asked how it should be with respect to (points of) the law which have not been (specially) mentioned, (the answer is), 'that which Brahmanas (who are) Sishtas propound, shall doubtlessly have legal (force).'

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मेणाधिगतो यैस् तु वेदः सपरिबृंहणः ।
ते शिष्टा ब्राह्मणा ज्ञेयाः श्रुतिप्रत्यक्षहेतवः ॥
verses.transliteration:
dharmeṇādhigato yais tu vedaḥ saparibṛṃhaṇaḥ |
te śiṣṭā brāhmaṇā jñeyāḥ śrutipratyakṣahetavaḥ ||
verses.translation: Those Brahmanas must be considered as Sishtas who, in accordance with the sacred law, have studied the Veda together with its appendages, and are able to adduce proofs perceptible by the senses from the revealed texts.

verses.sanskrit:
दशावराः वा परिषद् यं धर्मं परिकल्पयेत् ।
त्र्यवरा वापि वृत्तस्था तं धर्मं न विचालयेत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
daśāvarāḥ vā pariṣad yaṃ dharmaṃ parikalpayet |
tryavarā vāpi vṛttasthā taṃ dharmaṃ na vicālayet ||
verses.translation: Whatever an assembly, consisting either of at least ten, or of at least three persons who follow their prescribed occupations, declares to be law, the legal (force of) that one must not dispute.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रैविद्यो हेतुकस् तर्की नैरुतो धर्मपाठकः ।
त्र्यश् चाश्रमिणः पूर्वे परिषत् स्याद् दशावरा ॥
verses.transliteration:
traividyo hetukas tarkī nairuto dharmapāṭhakaḥ |
tryaś cāśramiṇaḥ pūrve pariṣat syād daśāvarā ||
verses.translation: Three persons who each know one of the three principal Vedas, a logician, a Mimamsaka, one who knows the Nirukta, one who recites (the Institutes of) the sacred law, and three men belonging to the first three orders shall constitute a (legal) assembly, consisting of at least ten members.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋग्वेदविद् यजुर्विच् च सामवेदविद् एव च ।
त्र्यवरा परिषद् ज्ञेया धर्मसंशयनिर्णये ॥
verses.transliteration:
ṛgvedavid yajurvic ca sāmavedavid eva ca |
tryavarā pariṣad jñeyā dharmasaṃśayanirṇaye ||
verses.translation: One who knows the Rig-veda, one who knows the Yagur-veda, and one who knows the Sama-veda, shall be known (to form) an assembly consisting of at least three members (and competent) to decide doubtful points of law.

verses.sanskrit:
एको ऽपि वेदविद् धर्मं यं व्यवस्येद् द्विजोत्तमः ।
स विज्ञेयः परो धर्मो नाज्ञानाम् उदितो ऽयुतैः ॥
verses.transliteration:
eko 'pi vedavid dharmaṃ yaṃ vyavasyed dvijottamaḥ |
sa vijñeyaḥ paro dharmo nājñānām udito 'yutaiḥ ||
verses.translation: Even that which one Brahmana versed in the Veda declares to be law, must be considered (to have) supreme legal (force, but) not that which is proclaimed by myriads of ignorant men.

verses.sanskrit:
अव्रतानाम् अमन्त्राणां जातिमात्रोपजीविनाम् ।
सहस्रशः समेतानां परिषत्त्वं न विद्यते ॥
verses.transliteration:
avratānām amantrāṇāṃ jātimātropajīvinām |
sahasraśaḥ sametānāṃ pariṣattvaṃ na vidyate ||
verses.translation: Even if thousands of Brahmanas, who have not fulfilled their sacred duties, are unacquainted with the Veda, and subsist only by the name of their caste, meet, they cannot (form) an assembly (for settling the sacred law).

verses.sanskrit:
यं वदन्ति तमोभूता मूर्खा धर्मम् अतद्विदः ।
तत् पापं शतधा भूत्वा तद्वक्तॄन् अनुगच्छति ॥
verses.transliteration:
yaṃ vadanti tamobhūtā mūrkhā dharmam atadvidaḥ |
tat pāpaṃ śatadhā bhūtvā tadvaktṝn anugacchati ||
verses.translation: The sin of him whom dunces, incarnations of Darkness, and unacquainted with the law, instruct (in his duty), falls, increased a hundredfold, on those who propound it.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद् वो ऽभिहितं सर्वं निःश्रेयसकरं परम् ।
अस्माद् अप्रच्युतो विप्रः प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
etad vo 'bhihitaṃ sarvaṃ niḥśreyasakaraṃ param |
asmād apracyuto vipraḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: All that which is most efficacious for securing supreme bliss has been thus declared to you; a Brahmana who does not fall off from that obtains the most excellent state.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स भगवान् देवो लोकानां हितकाम्यया ।
धर्मस्य परं गुह्यं ममेदं सर्वम् उक्तवान् ॥
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ sa bhagavān devo lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā |
dharmasya paraṃ guhyaṃ mamedaṃ sarvam uktavān ||
verses.translation: Thus did that worshipful deity disclose to me, through a desire of benefiting mankind, this whole most excellent secret of the sacred law.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वम् आत्मनि सम्पश्येत् सच् चासच् च समाहितः ।
सर्वं ह्य् आत्मनि सम्पश्यन् नाधर्मे कुरुते मतिम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
sarvam ātmani sampaśyet sac cāsac ca samāhitaḥ |
sarvaṃ hy ātmani sampaśyan nādharme kurute matim ||
verses.translation: Let (every Brahmana), concentrating his mind, fully recognise in the Self all things, both the real and the unreal, for he who recognises the universe in the Self, does not give his heart to unrighteousness.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मैव देवताः सर्वाः सर्वम् आत्मन्य् अवस्थितम् ।
आत्मा हि जनयत्य् एषां कर्मयोगं शरीरिणाम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ātmaiva devatāḥ sarvāḥ sarvam ātmany avasthitam |
ātmā hi janayaty eṣāṃ karmayogaṃ śarīriṇām ||
verses.translation: The Self alone is the multitude of the gods, the universe rests on the Self; for the Self produces the connexion of these embodied (spirits) with actions.

verses.sanskrit:
खं सन्निवेशयेत् खेषु चेष्टनस्पर्शने ऽनिलम् ।
पक्तिदृष्ट्योः परं तजः स्नेहे ऽपो गां च मूर्तिषु ॥
verses.transliteration:
khaṃ sanniveśayet kheṣu ceṣṭanasparśane 'nilam |
paktidṛṣṭyoḥ paraṃ tajaḥ snehe 'po gāṃ ca mūrtiṣu ||
verses.translation: Let him meditate on the ether as identical with the cavities (of the body), on the wind as identical with the organs of motions and of touch, on the most excellent light as the same with his digestive organs and his sight, on water as the same with the (corporeal) fluids, on the earth as the same with the solid parts (of his body);

verses.sanskrit:
मनसीन्दुं दिशः श्रोत्रे क्रान्ते विष्णुं बले हरम् ।
वाच्य् अग्निं मित्रम् उत्सर्गे प्रजने च प्रजापतिम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
manasīnduṃ diśaḥ śrotre krānte viṣṇuṃ bale haram |
vācy agniṃ mitram utsarge prajane ca prajāpatim ||
verses.translation: On the moon as one with the internal organ, on the quarters of the horizon as one with his sense of hearing, on Vishnu as one with his (power of) motion, on Hara as the same with his strength, on Agni (Fire) as identical with his speech, on Mitra as identical with his excretions, and on Pragapati as one with his organ of generation.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रशासितारं सर्वेषाम् अणीयांसम् अणोर् अपि ।
रुक्माभं स्वप्नधीगम्यं विद्यात् तं पुरुषं परम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇor api |
rukmābhaṃ svapnadhīgamyaṃ vidyāt taṃ puruṣaṃ param ||
verses.translation: Let him know the supreme Male (Purusha, to be) the sovereign ruler of them all, smaller even than small, bright like gold, and perceptible by the intellect (only when) in (a state of) sleep (-like abstraction).

verses.sanskrit:
एतम् एके वदन्त्य् अग्निं मनुम् अन्ये प्रजापतिम् ।
इन्द्रम् एके परे प्राणम् अपरे ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
etam eke vadanty agniṃ manum anye prajāpatim |
indram eke pare prāṇam apare brahma śāśvatam ||
verses.translation: Some call him Agni (Fire), others Manu, the Lord of creatures, others Indra, others the vital air, and again others eternal Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
एष सर्वाणि भूतानि पञ्चभिर् व्याप्य मूर्तिभिः ।
जन्मवृद्धिक्षयैर् नित्यं संसारयति चक्रवत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
eṣa sarvāṇi bhūtāni pañcabhir vyāpya mūrtibhiḥ |
janmavṛddhikṣayair nityaṃ saṃsārayati cakravat ||
verses.translation: He pervades all created beings in the five forms, and constantly makes them, by means of birth, growth and decay, revolve like the wheels (of a chariot).

verses.sanskrit:
एवं यः सर्वभूतेषु पश्यत्य् आत्मानम् आत्मना ।
स सर्वसमताम् एत्य ब्रह्माभ्येति परं पदम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūteṣu paśyaty ātmānam ātmanā |
sa sarvasamatām etya brahmābhyeti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: He who thus recognises the Self through the Self in all created beings, becomes equal (-minded) towards all, and enters the highest state, Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्य् एतन् मानवं शास्त्रं भृगुप्रोक्तं पठन् द्विजः ।
भवत्य् आचारवान् नित्यं यथेष्टां प्राप्नुयाद् गतिम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ity etan mānavaṃ śāstraṃ bhṛguproktaṃ paṭhan dvijaḥ |
bhavaty ācāravān nityaṃ yatheṣṭāṃ prāpnuyād gatim ||
verses.translation: A twice-born man who recites these Institutes, revealed by Manu, will be always virtuous in conduct, and will reach whatever condition he desires.
